title: Existing signed-line tensor theorem for unrestricted derived completeness
statement:
Let l be prime, E a finite-dimensional extension of Q_l, and X a scheme, allowing independent site and coefficient universes as in integralTowerModules. Let L be a finite locally free rank-one module over the completed integral coefficient sheaf on X. For every integer m and every unbounded derived object K, unrestricted derived completeness of K implies unrestricted derived completeness of its exact derived tensor with the signed power L^[m]. The signed powers, tensor functor and completeness predicate are the existing declarations CompletedLineTensor.power, CompletedLineTensor.tensor and IsDerivedCompleteUnrestricted. Precisely the existing Lean statement is:

theorem complete (L : integralTowerModules l E X) [L.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank 1]
    (m : ℤ) (K : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l E X))
    (hK : IsDerivedCompleteUnrestricted l E X K) :
    IsDerivedCompleteUnrestricted l E X ((tensor l E X L m).obj K)

proof.text: For each signed power P of L, the unbounded-line tensor theorem gives exact inverse tensor functors with the internal dual and their derived equivalences. An equivalence preserves countable products by their universal property: Hom(B,T(product M_n)) identifies with Hom(T^{-1}B,product M_n), hence with the product of Hom(B,T M_n). This comparison respects every projection. No assertion that restriction to a trivializing cover preserves products is used.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat representative for K. Tensoring with the exact line remains K-flat. The balancing map identifies the quotient reduction of its line twist with the line twist of its restricted quotient reduction: (x tensor p) tensor a maps to (x tensor a) tensor p. Its inverse reassociates the same factors. Use the derived tensor descent to pass these natural comparisons to the unbounded derived categories. The change-of-rings K-flat theorem justifies computing finite reductions this way; it does not claim that the restricted finite quotient is K-flat over the integral ring. Both maps commute with quotient transitions and with x mapped to 1 tensor x, as checked on tensor generators.

proof.text: Apply the triangulated line equivalence to the canonical augmented reduction Roos triangle witnessing unrestricted completeness. Use the product comparison of step 1 and augmented-tower comparison of step 2. The first arrow becomes precisely the canonical reduction-unit product map, and the second becomes 1 minus the quotient shift, by composing with each projection. Transport the connecting arrow through these isomorphisms. Distinguishedness is invariant under triangle isomorphism, giving the defining unrestricted completeness of the twist. This works for every integer power, every unbounded K, and independently sized site and coefficient universes.
